text: In short Choose a GEO agency by what it can show you, not by what it promises. Ask which prompts it tracks, what it changes on your site each month and who approves it. A promised top spot in AI answers is a red flag. scaile does Managed GEO, which makes it more than an agency: it combines the agility and personal service of an agency with software and analytics tools, and shows you all of it. Published Nov 3, 2026 Reading time 8 min Dora Pruteanu Founding Engineer Dora is a founding engineer at scaile. She studied computer science, psychology and neuroscience at TUM, which is the perfect fit for GEO: she has a deep understanding of technology and of the human side, and knows how to write and produce content that leads humans to buy and AI to show you in its answers. Key takeaways Count only what an agency can show you: the prompts it measures, a visibility share across many runs and every change it made to your site. Measure your own starting point before the first call. Without it, you cannot judge any answer you hear. A promised top spot in ChatGPT is a reason to leave, because AI answers change from one run to the next. Verify a case study by re-running a sample of its prompts yourself, not by reading the screenshot. Score every agency on your shortlist on the same sheet, with execution weighted highest, and put scaile through it too. How do you choose a GEO agency? You choose a GEO agency by testing whether it can show its work. A pitch deck shows outcomes. A good agency also shows the method: the buyer questions it measures, how often you appear across many runs, the pages it will change and who approves them. What it cannot show you, you cannot check later. That test works because GEO is mostly execution. The paper that named generative engine optimization reports that changing what a page says and how raised visibility in generative engine responses by up to 40% on its own benchmark. It is an arXiv preprint, not peer reviewed. [1] So the useful question is which agency will change the right pages on your site every month and prove what moved. This article assumes you have a shortlist. Whether you need an agency at all is covered in agency vs tool vs in-house vs DIY , and a month of agency work in what a GEO agency does . Your baseline before the first call Measure where you stand before you talk to anyone. Write down ten to twenty questions your buyers ask right before they choose a provider in your category, then check which brands AI answers name for them. The free AI Visibility Check runs ten real buying questions through ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity. You can also check your AI visibility by hand . The baseline you take before the first call is used twice: to judge the answers in the call and as the yardstick when you re-run a case study. With that baseline you can see whether a sample audit found the same competitors you did, and any promised growth has a number to be measured against. Also decide how many hours a week your team can give to reviews and approvals, then ask each agency how much time it needs from you. Which questions should you ask a GEO agency? Ask questions that force the agency to describe work, not results. Google’s own advice for hiring an SEO is a useful base. It suggests asking for examples of previous work, the results to expect in what timeframe and how success is measured. [2] It also suggests asking whether the agency will share every change it makes to your site, with the reasoning behind it. [2] For GEO, sharpen them like this: Which prompts would you track for us, and why those? A good answer names buyer questions from your category, says where they come from (search data, sales calls, AI fan-out queries) and separates questions that bring buyers from questions that bring impressions. How do you measure visibility? A good answer is a share of answers across many runs and several AI assistants, over time. A single position or one screenshot is a weak answer. What will you change on our site in the first month? A good answer names pages, page types and fixes. Who approves each change, and how? A good answer shows where you review content and sources before anything goes live. What happens to the content and data if we stop? A good answer: the pages, briefs and knowledge base stay yours. In regulated categories, also ask how the agency checks every claim before it goes live. Reviews on Clutch or Trustpilot show how clients felt about the service, not whether AI answers changed. Red flags that should end the conversation Some answers end the evaluation on the spot. Google’s guidance for SEO applies one to one: “No one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google.” It warns against anyone who claims to guarantee rankings or a “special relationship” with Google. [2] Five red flags for GEO: A guaranteed top spot in ChatGPT or any other AI answer. The next section explains why nobody can promise it. A secret method. Google advises caution if a company “is secretive or won’t clearly explain what they intend to do”. [2] GEO work can be explained in plain words. A special markup for AI Overviews. Google says there are “no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode, nor other special optimizations necessary”. [3] An agency selling one sells something Google says is not needed. Results you cannot reproduce. No prompt list, no dates, no assistant named: the number cannot be checked. Work that ends at the report. If nobody changes your pages, AI answers have no new reason to change. For what the main agencies actually offer, compare them in the scored list of GEO agencies and the DACH ranking . Why can nobody guarantee first place in ChatGPT? Nobody can guarantee first place because AI answers have no fixed positions. Google says AI Overviews and AI Mode may run several related searches across subtopics and data sources to build one response. It adds that the responses and links they show will vary. [3] The answer is assembled again for every request. SparkToro measured how much that varies. In its study, 600 volunteers ran 12 prompts through ChatGPT, Claude and Google’s AI a combined 2,961 times. [4] The chance that ChatGPT or Google’s AI gave the same list of brands in any two of 100 responses was below 1 in 100. Rand Fishkin’s conclusion: visibility share across many prompts, run many times, is a reasonable metric. Any tool that reports a “ranking position in AI” is not. [4] A screenshot is one answer out of many. Count how often a brand appears across many runs instead. So an honest agency promises work and a way to measure it, never a place. It reports how often your brand appeared across a fixed set of prompts, and how that share moved. A good AI visibility score is built the same way. How do you verify an agency’s case studies? Verify a case study by repeating part of it yourself. The four questions to put to every number are in how to check an AI SEO agency’s results . These five steps test the answers: 1 Ask for the prompt list Get the prompts behind the result, the assistants and the date range. Your part Pick five to ten prompts from the list 2 Re-run a sample Ask those prompts in a clean session, several times each, in each assistant named. Your part Count how often the client’s brand appears 3 Compare the share Your count will not match the agency’s figure exactly, because answers vary. It should land in the same range. Your part Note large gaps and ask about them 4 Check the site Look at the client’s pages the agency says it changed. The work should be visible and live. Your part Ask what changed and when 5 Talk to the client Ask for a reference call with the person who approved the work. Your part Ask what their team had to do each week A case study that cannot share its prompts is a story, not evidence. A scoring sheet for your shortlist Score every agency from 1 to 5 on the same criteria, with weights fixed before the first call. Execution weighs most because it is the part that changes AI answers. Criterion Suggested weight What earns a 5 Execution on your site 25% Names the pages and fixes for month one; publishes with your approval Prompt selection 20% Buyer questions from data, with reasons; you see the full list Measurement 20% Visibility share across runs and assistants; you can re-run it Verifiable case studies 15% Prompt lists, live pages and a reference call Fit with your team 10% Clear weekly time from you; approval flow you can live with Ownership and exit 10% Content, briefs and data stay yours Prices belong next to this sheet, not in it: compare them with what generative engine optimization costs once the scores are in. The best GEO agency for you is the one whose work you can see, check and own. Take your baseline, your questions and this sheet into every call, and drop the agencies that cannot answer. If nobody on your team has the hours to run GEO, talk to scaile about We run it : put the same questions to scaile first. FAQ Should I hire my existing SEO agency for GEO? Only if it passes the same questions and the same scoring sheet as a specialist. Some SEO agencies already do this work; others relabel their existing reports. How long should I give an agency before judging it? Agree on the prompts and the measurement first, then review the share every month. Expect visible work on your site within the first month, even if the share moves later. Sources 2311.09735 GEO: Generative Engine Optimization Do You Need an SEO? An AEO agency (answer engine optimization agency) helps your brand get mentioned, cited and recommended in AI answers from ChatGPT, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, Gemini, Perplexity and Claude. What does an AEO agency do? An AEO agency measures how AI answers describe your brand, fixes what stops AI systems from finding or trusting your pages, creates content worth citing, and earns mentions on the third-party sites AI already relies on. GEO (generative engine optimization) agencies and AI SEO agencies sell the same work. Much of it overlaps with SEO. Google's guide to optimizing for generative AI features says optimizing for generative AI search "is optimizing for the search experience, and thus still SEO." What's new is measuring answers platform by platform; our explainer on what AEO is covers the basics. What a real AEO engagement delivers Deliverable What good looks like AI visibility baseline Results per platform, with the prompt list attached Prompt research 100 or more prompts from sales calls, support tickets and Search Console Technical access AI crawler rules, indexing and rendering checked and fixed Answer-ready content Comparison, use-case and FAQ pages, plus refreshes of stale ones Off-site evidence Digital PR, real reviews, expert quotes and accurate listings Brand accuracy A log of wrong AI facts found, traced to a source and fixed Reporting Per-platform trends tied to the work shipped What a real AEO engagement delivers Off-site work matters more than most teams expect. In our study of where new brands earn AI authority , independent sources such as publications, directories, reviews and communities made up 67.7% of ChatGPT and 77.6% of Google AI citation activity. The brands' own sites made up 1.1% and 0.5%. How much does an AEO agency cost? As of October 2026, agencies that publish prices charge about $1,000 to more than $15,000 a month, and one-off audits cost a few hundred to several thousand dollars. There's no independent benchmark yet, so be wary of any single "average" price. Four agencies we read publish AEO or GEO pricing on their own sites. We're not naming them, but this is what their pricing pages said on 26 October 2026. Published AEO and GEO agency pricing, as of 26 October 2026 Agency type Entry offer Monthly price Term Price scales with Productized AI visibility and SEO service $299 diagnostic $999 to $3,999 Month to month Pages optimized, assets, outreach, prompts tracked B2B content and SEO agency Monthly plans only $3,000 to $15,000 Month to month; discounts for 6 or 12 months Articles, refreshes, depth of AI citation tracking AI search agency in Europe €4,370 diagnostic, credited if you sign within 14 days From €6,995 (6-month rate) to €15,995 and up Month to month with 30 days' notice Content volume, landing pages, team size Full-service digital agency Two-month setup, $8,600 to $21,400 $2,900 to $9,200 after setup 6-month commitment Keywords, prompts targeted (100 to 250), pages Published AEO and GEO agency pricing, as of 26 October 2026 All four bundle AI search work with SEO and content work, and none offers pay-for-results pricing. Three other agencies we read publish no prices at all. These are the engagement models you'll see most: Audit or diagnostic: a one-off baseline and roadmap, sometimes credited to month one if you sign quickly. Monthly retainer: the most common model, priced by output such as articles, refreshes and outreach. Project or advisory: a fixed scope, such as a technical clean-up, or strategy time while your team does the work. Agency plus platform: ask whose name the account is in and whether tool fees are marked up. To compare quotes, list each one's monthly deliverables side by side. A cheaper retainer that ships half as much isn't cheaper. Red flags when hiring an AEO agency Walk away from guarantees, secret methods and manufactured mentions. Google, OpenAI and the FTC have each spelled out why. Guaranteed placement in AI answers. Google's advice on hiring an SEO says "No one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google," and its AI guide adds that "No third-party tool has access to our internal ranking or AI systems." OpenAI says advertisers have no ability to shape, rank, or alter ChatGPT's responses, so doubt any agency that claims it can. Claimed inside access. Google warns about SEOs who claim a "special relationship" with Google. Apply the same test to claims about any AI company. No per-platform reporting. In our AI Recognition Gap research , ChatGPT correctly identified the tracked brands in 95.0% of answers that named them, while Google AI did so in 56.8%. A blended score hides both. Black-box "AI hacks." Google says that for Google Search you can ignore "chunking" content, unnecessary AI text files like llms.txt, and pursuing inauthentic mentions. If an agency can't explain its method plainly, you can't judge it. Fake mentions and seeded posts. Google's spam policies define spam to include "attempting to manipulate generative AI responses in Google Search." They also list paying for links or for posts that contain links, and spammy forum posts, as spam. Bought or fake reviews. The FTC's final rule on fake reviews and testimonials bans fake reviews, paying for reviews that must be positive or negative, undisclosed insider reviews and fake social media indicators. Mass AI-written pages. Google counts "using generative AI tools or other similar tools to generate many pages without adding value for users" as scaled content abuse. Secrecy and lock-in. No change log, a request for write access to Search Console, a prompt set you never see, or 12 months with no exit. One question that filters fast: Ask every agency: "What won't you do?" Good agencies answer right away: no guarantees, no fake reviews, no seeded forum posts, no paid links passed off as editorial. Green flags: what a good AEO agency looks like Good agencies are specific about the work, honest about the overlap with SEO, and happy to be measured. They ask about your buyers, sales calls and support tickets before pitching. They back their advice with official documentation, as Google's hiring page suggests you check. They start off-site work from the sources AI already cites in your category. They hand over the prompt set, data and accounts in writing, and propose a short trial. 18 questions to ask an AEO agency before you sign Ask these early, then score the answers with the rubric below. Several come from Google's own hiring checklist, which now names "AEO" and "GEO" services. 18 questions to ask before hiring an AEO agency # Question A good answer 1 Which AI platforms will you track, and will you report each separately? Worked example: an agency scores 4 on measurement (20 points), 4 on deliverables (16), 3 on off-site evidence (9), 3 on reporting (9), 4 on transparency (12) and 2 on terms (4). That's 70, so push for a shorter term and data ownership in writing before signing. AEO agency vs in-house vs platform: which do you need? Decide by who will do the work every week. An agency sells people's time, while a platform sells data and capacity your team still has to direct and approve. How to run a 90-day AEO agency trial Agree on the prompts and metrics before day 1, take a per-platform baseline in the first two weeks, let the agency ship for about two months, and judge day 90 against that baseline. Put all of it in the contract. Judge the agency on what it shipped and on per-platform movement against your day-14 baseline. Before day 1: agree on the rules. Fix the prompt set (100 or more, branded and unbranded), platforms, metrics, read-only access and data ownership. In our research, growing a tracked set from 10 to 100 questions cut variation in reported brand coverage by about 73%. Days 1 to 14: take a baseline. Record mentions, citations, share of voice and answer accuracy for each platform. Run a free AI visibility report too, as a second view on the agency's numbers. Days 15 to 30: plan and fix. Expect a roadmap, technical fixes and corrections to wrong brand facts, but not big movement: one agency's pricing page says onboarding alone typically takes 30 to 45 days. Days 31 to 75: ship the work. Check shipped pages, refreshes and outreach against the plan every week. Days 76 to 90: read and decide. Compare each platform with its baseline, separate platform-wide shifts from brand problems, then continue, change scope or stop. Use first-party data wherever it exists. Search Console's Generative AI performance reports , live for all websites since August 31, 2026, show impressions, pages, countries, devices and dates for AI Overviews, AI Mode and Discover. Bing's AI Performance report , in public preview, shows citations across Microsoft Copilot and Bing's AI summaries. For ChatGPT, OpenAI's publisher and developer FAQ says it adds utm_source=chatgpt.com to referral URLs, so you can split that traffic out in analytics. How to work with an AEO agency well Treat the agency as part of your team: give it access, context and fast approvals. Budget your own time. One agency's pricing page estimates 6 to 8 hours of client time in the first 30 days, then about 2 to 3 hours a month. Name one owner who can approve work within an agreed time, such as two working days. Share raw inputs like sales call notes, support tickets and Search Console queries. That's where the best prompts come from. Don't pay twice for tools. If the agency runs a platform, agree who pays and who owns the account. Where to find an AEO agency Build a shortlist of three to five, then run each through the 18 questions and the rubric. Lantern's GEO and AI Search Agency Directory is one place to start. In-house teams use it to track AI visibility per platform and have agents turn gaps into review-ready content that a person approves. It's built for agencies too. Lantern for agencies includes multi-client dashboards and white-label reports, and the Agency plan is $399 a month for three client workspaces, five agency seats and 1,000 Agent Runs, with more available as add-ons. To see where you stand before you talk to any agency, get a free AI Visibility Report . If you'd rather try a platform first, Lantern's free plan gives you ChatGPT tracking and 10 Agent Runs a month at $0. Frequently asked questions What is an AEO agency? An AEO agency works to get your brand mentioned, cited and recommended in AI answers. Typical services include AI visibility tracking, technical fixes for AI crawlers, answer-ready content, digital PR and per-platform reporting. Is AEO legit? Yes, if you treat it as an extension of SEO rather than a bag of tricks. Google says optimizing for its AI features is still SEO. The genuinely new parts are measuring AI answers per platform and building evidence on third-party sites. Can you pay for AEO? You can pay an agency or a platform to do AEO work, and you can buy clearly labeled ads in ChatGPT. You can't pay to be placed inside the answer itself: OpenAI says ads don't influence ChatGPT's answers. How much does an AEO agency cost? Among agencies that publish prices, retainers ran from about $1,000 to more than $15,000 a month as of October 2026. Price mostly tracks output, so compare quotes by deliverables, not the headline fee. What's the difference between an AEO agency, a GEO agency and an AI SEO agency? Mostly the label. Google describes AEO and GEO as terms for work focused on visibility in AI search experiences, and AI SEO is used the same way. Judge an agency by its deliverables and reporting, not its acronym. What is the best AEO agency for B2B? There's no single best one, only the best fit for your category, budget and team. For B2B, look for experience with long sales cycles, comparison and use-case content, and reporting that ties AI referral visits to pipeline in your CRM.

text: ← Back to Blog How to Choose a GEO Agency in 2026: 142 Case Studies By Le Tuan Binh 16 min read · Last updated November 7, 2026 On this page ▾ The short answer 1. Decide how GEO fits with your SEO 2. Choose the AI platforms that matter to you 3. Ask what the agency measures, and how 4. Ask what AI visibility turned into 5. Know what a realistic result looks like 6. Ask where each result started 7. Check how much GEO the agency has done 8. Get the fee and what it covers in writing 9. Plan for about six months 10. Vet the case studies Before you sign 10 questions to ask a GEO agency Red flags when hiring a GEO agency When not to hire a GEO agency Find a GEO agency Related guides Methodology FAQs Generative engine optimization (GEO) is the work of getting a brand cited and recommended in AI answers: Google AI Overviews and AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini and the rest. It is new, the tools that measure it are new, and many agencies have only just started selling it. That makes it harder than usual to tell good proof from a good pitch. This guide shows what to check, in 10 steps. Each step comes from 142 GEO case studies published by 68 agencies and indexed in OpenServed's directory. We counted what agencies report, what they leave out, what a typical published result looks like and how long it took, so every piece of advice comes with evidence. Data as of November 2026. The full numbers are in GEO Statistics 2026 . The short answer Decide how GEO fits with your SEO. 90% of GEO case studies also list SEO, and only one of 142 lists GEO alone. Choose the AI platforms that matter to your customers. 25% of case studies name Google AI Overviews and 10% ChatGPT; 66% name no platform at all. Ask what the agency measures, and how. 27% of GEO case studies report no AI metric, and only 2 of 142 say how many prompts were tracked. Ask what AI visibility turned into. Only 13% tie AI search to leads or revenue. Know what a realistic result looks like. The median published case study reports a 188% increase in AI referral traffic and 158% in AI visibility, from small starting points. Ask where each result started. 16% of AI gains are 1,000% or more, and only 5.6% of case studies give an AI number before and after. Check how much GEO the agency has done. 40 of the 68 agencies have published one GEO case study, and only one has ten or more. Get the fee and what it covers in writing. None of the 142 case studies states a budget. Plan for about six months. The median GEO result is measured over 6 months, the same as SEO, and only 15% within 3 months. Vet the case studies. 34% carry none of five basic trust signals, and 16% are Client-verified, the highest share of any service we've studied. 1. Decide how GEO fits with your SEO GEO is sold as part of SEO. 90% of GEO case studies also list SEO, and only one of the 142 lists GEO alone. The average GEO case study lists 2.8 services, more than for any other service we've studied. Content is the next most common partner. Content marketing appears alongside GEO in 25% of case studies, PPC in 19% and local SEO in 11%. The two share most of the work. AI answers draw heavily on pages that already rank and on content that answers questions clearly. That is why most agencies treat GEO as an extension of SEO and content, not a separate product. What to do: decide first whether you want GEO from your current SEO agency or team, or from a second agency. If it's a second one, ask how the work will fit together and who owns what: technical fixes, content, digital PR and tracking. Be wary of GEO sold as a separate product that ignores your existing search work. 2. Choose the AI platforms that matter to you Google AI Overviews dominate. 25% of GEO case studies name Google AI Overviews or AI Mode in their results. ChatGPT appears in 10%, Perplexity and Gemini in 4% each, Claude in 2% and Copilot in 1%. Two in three name no platform. 66% of GEO case studies report AI results without saying which AI tool they come from, using terms like "AI visibility" or "AI referral traffic". What to do: before you talk to agencies, find out where your customers ask questions. Then ask each agency which platforms it will report on separately. Being cited in Google AI Overviews and being recommended in ChatGPT are different results, won in different ways. 3. Ask what the agency measures, and how 27% of GEO case studies report no AI metric at all. 38 of the 142 list GEO as a service but report only traditional SEO results, such as organic traffic or rankings. There is no standard measure yet. Only 45% of AI search results state a percentage change. The rest are counts or levels, such as a number of appearances in AI Overviews or a visibility score across a set of prompts, each from the agency's own tool. The method is rarely shown. GEO is measured by running a fixed set of prompts (the questions your customers ask an AI tool) and checking whether your brand appears. Only 5 of the 142 case studies mention tracked prompts, and only 2 say how many: one more than 180, the other more than 1,500. 0.7% report share of voice in AI answers. What to do: ask which tool the agency uses, which prompts it will track and how they were chosen, how often it checks, and how it will measure AI referral traffic in your analytics. Get a baseline before the work starts, and ask for the prompt list in writing. 4. Ask what AI visibility turned into Most GEO case studies stop at visibility. 37% report AI visibility, citations or mentions and no AI traffic or AI-driven result. 27% report AI referral traffic. Only 13% tie AI search to leads or revenue. 19 of the 142 report leads, sign-ups or sales attributed to AI. Among case studies that report any AI metric, 44% also report leads, conversions or revenue of any kind. Leads and revenue from AI are too few to measure. Only 8 case studies state a percentage gain in leads or revenue attributed to AI, too few for a reliable median. What to do: ask how the agency will connect AI visibility to traffic, then to leads or sales: how it tags AI referral traffic, and how it attributes enquiries that started in an AI answer. A citation that sends no one to your site is hard to value. 5. Know what a realistic result looks like The median GEO case study reports a 188% increase in AI referral traffic. Among the 25 case studies that state one, half fall between 78% and 720%. The median increase in AI visibility, citations or mentions is 158% (30 case studies). AI gains are large because the starting point is small. AI referral traffic barely registered for most sites a year or two ago, so even a few extra visits show up as a big percentage. Traditional search results are more modest. The median reported increase in organic traffic is 82% (34 case studies). The median gain in conversions or leads is 164% (36), and those results aren't attributed to AI. These are the wins. Agencies publish the programs that went well, and GEO is new, so these figures rest on few data points. Treat them as early signals, not benchmarks. What to do: ask an agency what result it expects, from what starting point, and what that estimate is based on. Be wary of a promised percentage, or a guarantee that AI tools will cite you: no one controls what an AI model says. 6. Ask where each result started Starting points are almost never shown. Only 5.6% of GEO case studies give an AI number before and after, and 2.8% say the starting point was zero. A 1,000% gain from 10 visits a month is 110 visits, and 16% of AI gains are 1,000% or more. The method behind the number is missing too. 3.5% mention the prompts they tracked, 1.4% say how many, and none say how long the program ran or what it cost. What to do: for any AI result an agency shows you, ask for the number before and after, not only the percentage, and the dates of each. Ask to see the prompts behind a visibility score. 7. Check how much GEO the agency has done GEO is new for almost every agency. 68 of the 330 agencies in our directory have published a GEO case study. 40 of them have published one, 52 two or fewer, and only one has ten or more. GEO is a small part of most agencies' work. Of the 59 agencies that have ten or more case studies in total and list GEO, 3 have it in at least a quarter of them. The proof is spread thin. Coalition Technologies, TripleDart Digital and WebFX account for 20% of the GEO case studies, with 16, 7 and 6. What to do: ask how many GEO programs the agency has run, for how long, and to see the results of more than one. An agency with strong SEO work and one early GEO case study may still be a good choice, but know that you are part of its learning. 8. Get the fee and what it covers in writing None of the 142 GEO case studies states a budget, so we can't tell you what a fair price is. The price ranges on other guides are not sourced, and they disagree: one lists $7,000 to $15,000 a month for mid-market programs, another £3,000 to £10,000. GEO is usually sold in three ways: A one-off audit, which checks how often AI tools mention you today, for which prompts, and what to fix. A monthly retainer, which covers tracking, content, technical fixes and digital PR over time. A project, such as rebuilding key pages so AI tools can read and quote them. Tracking tools are a separate cost. Many agencies use a paid AI visibility tool; ask whether its fee is included and whether you keep access if you leave. What to do: compare quotes on what they cover, not on the monthly figure. Ask each agency to list the prompts and platforms it will track, the content and fixes it will deliver each month, how often you get a report, and the notice period. 9. Plan for about six months The median GEO result is measured over 6 months. 26 of the 142 case studies state a period in days, weeks, months or years, and the median is 6 months, the same as for SEO. Fast results are rare. Only 15% of those results came within 3 months. 73% came within 6 months, and 27% took longer. This is longer than some guides promise. Competitor pages quote 60 to 120 days for a lift in AI citations, without a source. In published case studies, most results are reported after three months or more. What to do: agree on a baseline in month one and a review at about month six, with milestones in between: prompts tracked, pages fixed, first citations. Be wary of citations promised within weeks. 10. Vet the case studies We checked each GEO case study for five trust signals: a business result (such as leads, sales or revenue), a number before and after, a time period, a client quote, and Client-verified status. 34% carry none of the five. That is fewer than the 41% across all services, but it still means one in three GEO case studies gives you nothing to check. Only 9.9% carry three or more. 16% of GEO case studies are Client-verified. That is 23 of 142, from 18 agencies, the highest share of any service we've studied. On OpenServed, Client-verified means the client has confirmed the results. Everything else is as reported by the agency. Verified case studies are more likely to report an AI metric. 83% of verified GEO case studies report one, against 71% of agency-reported ones. What to do: ask whether you can speak with the client behind a case study. Then test it yourself: run a few of the tracked prompts in the AI tools that matter to you and see whether the client appears. Before you sign Get these in writing, and make sure you own them: The prompt list: the questions that will be tracked, on which platforms, and how often. The baseline: where you stand today on each prompt, and your AI referral traffic. Tracking access: logins to the AI visibility tool, or an export of the data each month. Analytics: AI referral traffic tagged in your own analytics account, not only in the agency's reports. Content: the pages and articles the agency writes are yours, including after the contract ends. 10 questions to ask a GEO agency Each question below comes from one of the 10 steps. A good answer is specific; a warning sign is a claim with nothing behind it. How does GEO fit with our SEO? A good answer is one plan, with clear roles if another agency runs SEO. A warning sign is GEO sold as a separate product that ignores SEO. Which AI platforms will you report on? A good answer names them and reports each separately. A warning sign is "AI search" with no platform. What will you measure, and how? A good answer names the tool, the tracked prompt list, how often it checks, and a baseline. A warning sign is a visibility score with no method behind it. What did AI visibility turn into? A good answer shows AI referral traffic, leads or sales, tracked. A warning sign is mentions and citations on their own. What result should we expect? A good answer is a range tied to clients like you, with the starting point. A warning sign is a guaranteed citation or a promised percentage. Where did each result start? A good answer gives a number before and after, with dates. A warning sign is a four-digit percentage with no starting point. How many GEO programs have you run? A good answer is several, with results you can check. A warning sign is one case study, or none, behind the pitch. What will we pay, and what does it cover? A good answer is a written fee with the prompts, platforms, content and reports it covers. A warning sign is a cheap "unlimited GEO" package. How long until we see results? A good answer is a baseline in month one and a verdict by about month six. A warning sign is citations promised within weeks. Can we check a result ourselves? A good answer is prompts you can run and a client you can call. A warning sign is no prompts to test and no reference. Red flags when hiring a GEO agency A guaranteed citation or ranking in AI answers. No one controls what an AI model says. GEO with no AI metric. 27% of GEO case studies report only SEO results. Visibility with nothing after it. 37% report AI visibility and no traffic or leads from AI. A four-digit percentage with no starting point. 16% of AI gains are 1,000% or more, and only 5.6% of case studies show the before and after. "AI search" with no platform. 66% of case studies name no AI platform. A score you can't check. Only 2 of 142 case studies say how many prompts were tracked. Citations promised within weeks. The median published result is measured over 6 months. A tool or prompt list you can't access. If you leave, you should keep your baseline and your data. When not to hire a GEO agency GEO builds on SEO, so a GEO agency may not be your first hire: If your site has weak SEO basics, such as pages that don't rank or can't be crawled, fix those first. AI answers draw heavily on pages that already rank. If you already have a good SEO agency, ask it to add AI tracking and GEO before hiring a second agency. 90% of GEO case studies come from agencies that also do SEO. If your customers don't use AI tools to choose a provider like you, check that first: run your customers' questions in AI tools and see what comes back. A GEO specialist makes more sense when AI answers already shape your market, your SEO is in good shape, and you want someone to own AI visibility and its tracking. Find a GEO agency OpenServed's GEO agency directory lists agencies by the case studies they have published, so you can check each of the steps above before you make contact. You can narrow it to small business or enterprise . Look for the Client-verified badge on results the client has confirmed. Related guides How to choose an SEO agency , since most GEO is sold with SEO. How to choose a content marketing agency , since AI answers draw on content. GEO Statistics 2026 , for the full data behind this guide. Methodology Source: the 142 case studies in OpenServed's directory that list GEO as a service, from 68 agencies, as of November 2026. Comparisons across services use all 7,721 case studies from 330 agencies. AI search metrics: a stat counts as an AI search metric when it mentions AI, AI Overviews, AI Mode, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Claude, Copilot, LLMs, generative or answer engines. We split these into AI referral traffic, AI visibility (citations, mentions, appearances or answers) and leads or revenue from AI. Medians: medians use stats that state a percentage change, one per case study (the first listed). The middle half runs from the 25th to the 75th percentile. Time period: a case study states a period when it says the result came in, within, after or over a number of days, weeks, months or years. When it gives several, we use the shortest. Trust signals: a business result (leads, sales, revenue, conversions, bookings, orders, sign-ups, calls or customers), a number before and after, a time period, a client quote, and Client-verified status. Bundled services: almost all of these case studies list other services alongside GEO, most often SEO, so results can't be attributed to GEO alone. Pricing: no case study states a budget. Price ranges mentioned in this guide come from other published guides and are not sourced. Selection bias: agencies publish their wins, and the directory is not a random sample. Agency-reported: except for the 23 Client-verified case studies, results are as published by each agency. Cite this data: OpenServed, "How to Choose a GEO Agency in 2026: 142 Case Studies", November 2026, https://openserved.com/blog/how-to-choose-a-geo-agency FAQs How do I choose a GEO agency? Check 10 things: how GEO fits with your SEO, which AI platforms it reports on, what it measures and how, what AI visibility turned into, whether its expected result is realistic, where each result started, how much GEO it has done, what the fee covers, the timeline, and whether its case studies can be checked. What does a GEO agency do? It works to get your brand cited and recommended in AI answers, such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini. The work usually covers tracking a set of prompts, fixing pages so AI tools can read and quote them, writing content that answers questions clearly, and earning mentions on other sites. Is GEO different from SEO? The work overlaps heavily. 90% of GEO case studies also list SEO, and only one of 142 lists GEO alone. GEO adds tracking and optimizing for AI answers on top of search and content work. Should I hire a GEO specialist or ask my SEO agency? If you already have a good SEO agency, ask it to add AI tracking and GEO first. A specialist makes more sense when AI answers already shape your market, your SEO is in good shape, and you want someone to own AI visibility. What results should I expect from a GEO agency? The median published case study reports a 188% increase in AI referral traffic and a 158% increase in AI visibility. These gains start from small numbers and come from agencies' best work, so a typical program is likely to land lower. How long does GEO take to work? The median published GEO result is measured over 6 months, the same as SEO. Only 15% of results that state a period came within 3 months. How much does a GEO agency cost? None of the 142 case studies we analyzed states a budget, and published price ranges are unsourced and disagree. Ask each agency for its fee in writing, with the prompts, platforms, content and reports it covers, and whether tracking tools are included. Which AI platforms should GEO target? The ones your customers use. In published case studies, Google AI Overviews are named most (25%), followed by ChatGPT (10%). Ask the agency to report each platform separately. How do you measure GEO results? With a tracked set of prompts, AI visibility or citation counts, and AI referral traffic in your analytics, all against a baseline. There is no standard yet: only 2 of 142 GEO case studies say how many prompts they tracked. Can a GEO agency guarantee my brand appears in ChatGPT? No. AI answers change by question, user and model version, and no one controls them. Be wary of any guarantee. text: Jul 16, 2026 GEO Agencies & Services: How to Choose a Generative Engine Optimization Partner Generative engine optimization has crossed the line from experiment to service category. Brands are hiring agencies to get them mentioned by ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity the way they once hired agencies for Google rankings, and a wave of providers has appeared to meet the demand, ranging from excellent to purely opportunistic. This guide covers what GEO services actually include, when hiring an agency beats doing it in-house, and how to tell the serious providers from the ones selling repackaged SEO. What GEO Services Actually Cover A complete generative engine optimization engagement has four parts: Measurement. Establishing where the brand stands: which prompts mention it, at what rate, against which competitors, across which AI engines. Everything else depends on this baseline, which is why serious providers start here rather than with content. Source strategy. Identifying the pages AI models cite in the category (review platforms, comparison sites, communities, editorial rankings) and building a plan to earn presence on them. In most categories, a small set of heavily-cited pages controls the answers. Content work. Creating and restructuring content so models can extract and cite it: direct answers to buyer questions, comparison pages, structured data, and coverage of the topics where the measurement shows gaps. Ongoing tracking. AI answers shift with model updates and new content. Monthly reporting on mention rates, competitor movement, and source changes is what separates a program from a one-off project. If a proposal is missing the first or last part, you're buying content production, not GEO. Agency, In-House, or Tooling? The honest answer is that the measurement layer is a platform problem, not a people problem: no agency can hand-check hundreds of prompts across three engines and multiple markets every day. The real question is who acts on the data. In-house with a platform fits teams that already own SEO and content. AI visibility tracking plugs into the existing workflow, and the platform's weekly reporting replaces the agency retainer. Agency plus platform fits teams without content capacity, or agencies already running the brand's SEO. The agency executes the source and content strategy; the platform keeps both sides honest about whether it's working. Agency alone , without measurement, is the arrangement to avoid. Neither side can tell whether the work moved anything. Red Flags When Evaluating GEO Providers Guaranteed placement. Nobody can guarantee that ChatGPT will recommend a brand. Answers are probabilistic and change with model updates. A provider promising "#1 in ChatGPT" is promising something they don't control. No baseline measurement. If the engagement starts with content deliverables instead of an audit of current visibility, sources, and competitors, the strategy is generic by construction. SEO deliverables with new labels. Keyword rankings and domain authority are not AI visibility metrics. The relevant numbers are mention rate, position in answers, competitor share, and citation sources. One-time optimization. A brand's AI visibility a month after the project ends is the only result that matters, and it requires ongoing tracking by definition. Questions That Sort the Field Quickly Which prompts will you track for us, and how did you choose them? Which sources currently drive AI answers in our category? How do you measure results, and can we see the dashboard ourselves? What happened to your other clients' mention rates over six months? Strong providers answer all four with specifics. Weak ones pivot to content volume and publishing cadence. Where to Find Agencies That Already Do This We maintain a partner directory of agencies and consultants who run their clients' AI visibility programs on GetMentioned, which means they work measurement-first by default: every recommendation they make is tested against real prompt-level tracking across ChatGPT, Gemini, and Perplexity. If you're a brand, it's a shortlist of providers whose work you can verify in the data. If you're an agency building a GEO practice, the partner program is how you get listed. Frequently Asked Questions What does GEO cost compared to SEO? Engagements currently mirror SEO retainers, typically from around €1,000 per month for a consultant-led program to five figures for multi-market enterprise work. The tooling layer is separate and comparatively cheap; AI visibility tracking starts at €89 per month, which is also why measurement is worth owning even if you outsource execution. Do I need a GEO agency if I already have an SEO agency? Often your SEO agency can become your GEO provider, since the disciplines overlap heavily on content and authority building. What they need is the measurement layer and category source data. Pointing them at the answers your buyers actually see is a faster path than hiring a second agency. How long until GEO work shows results? Source-level wins (getting added to a heavily-cited comparison page, for example) can show up in answers within weeks. Category-level visibility shifts typically take one to two quarters of consistent work. Anyone quoting days is measuring something other than AI answers. text: On this page Hire an AI SEO agency that can show you exactly how it measures brand mentions and citations in ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews, explains every change it makes to your site, and refuses to guarantee placement. Google’s own hiring guidance says no one can guarantee a #1 ranking, and AI answers are even less predictable than rankings. Nearly every agency has added “AI” to its homepage lately, so the label tells you very little. I run the AI search practice at Sentic, and we’re an AI search optimization agency , so read this knowing that. I’ve tried to write the questions so they work just as well on us as on anyone else. Below you’ll find what the service should include, 12 questions to ask on the sales call, the red flags that should end the conversation, a scorecard you can copy into a spreadsheet, and a realistic timeline for results. Are AEO, GEO and AI SEO different services? No, for buying purposes they’re the same service with different names. Answer engine optimization (AEO), generative engine optimization (GEO), AI SEO, LLM optimization and AI visibility all describe the work of getting your brand named and cited in answers generated by AI tools. The terms came from different places. GEO comes from academic research: a 2023 paper by Aggarwal and colleagues, “GEO: Generative Engine Optimization” , found that GEO methods can boost visibility by up to 40% in generative engine responses. AEO grew out of the featured snippet and voice search era. AI SEO is mostly what buyers type into Google. If an agency tells you GEO and AEO are fundamentally different disciplines and you need both, ask what changes in the actual deliverables. In my experience the answer is usually “the invoice.” Our AI search glossary covers the vocabulary if you want to check whether a proposal is using terms precisely or decoratively. What matters more than the label is the relationship to traditional SEO. On the Google side especially, AI search is SEO with extra steps. Google states plainly that there are no additional requirements to appear in AI Overviews or AI Mode , nor other special optimizations necessary, beyond being indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. So an AI SEO agency that can’t do solid technical and content SEO is building on sand. Our guide on how to choose an SEO agency covers that side of the evaluation. What should an AI SEO agency actually deliver? An AI SEO agency should deliver four things: a measured baseline of your AI visibility, a prioritized plan tied to the questions your buyers ask, the on-site and off-site work to execute that plan, and recurring reporting that separates mentions from citations. If any of those four is missing, you’re buying part of a service. Here’s what each piece looks like in practice. Deliverable What good looks like What weak looks like Baseline A fixed prompt set run across named AI engines, with your mention and citation share recorded against competitors before any work starts A few screenshots of ChatGPT answers, no competitors, no repeatable method Prompt and keyword research Questions mapped to real buyer stages, refreshed each quarter A keyword list from three years ago with “AI” added to the title On-site work Fixing thin pages, heading structure, internal links, indexation, and rewriting key pages so they answer questions directly Adding new files or schema types and calling it optimization Off-site work Earning accurate coverage in the third-party sources AI tools already cite for your category Mass posting on forums or buying listicle placements Reporting Mentions, citations, AI referral traffic and leads or revenue, with the change log next to the numbers Activity counts: “we made 140 optimizations this month” The distinction between mentions and citations matters more than most proposals admit. A mention is when the AI names your brand in the answer. A citation is when it links to your site as a source. You can have plenty of one and almost none of the other, which is why our State of AI Visibility 2026 study tracks them separately across 55 brands. For a worked example of how we structure this: our AEO program tracks five AI engines (ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity, Google AI Overviews and AI Mode) and two metrics (mentions and citations), benchmarked against that 55-brand dataset. You don’t need to copy our setup. You should expect any agency to describe its own setup with the same level of specificity. What are the 12 questions to ask an AI SEO agency? Ask these 12 questions on the first or second call, and pay attention to how specific the answers are. Vague answers to measurement questions are the most reliable warning sign I know of. Several of these are adapted from Google’s own advice on hiring an SEO , which still holds up well for AI search. Which AI engines do you track, and how? A good answer names the engines and explains the method: a fixed set of prompts, run on a schedule, with results stored so they can be compared over time. A weak answer is “we monitor AI search.” Do you report mentions and citations separately? They behave differently and need different fixes. An agency that lumps them into one “AI visibility score” can’t tell you which problem you have. How do you build the prompt set, and how often does it change? Prompts should come from real buyer questions, sales calls and search data, not from the agency’s imagination. They should be reviewed at least quarterly, because the questions people ask keep moving. What will my baseline look like before you start? Ask to see a sample baseline report. If they can’t show one, they probably don’t build one, and without a baseline any later “improvement” is unverifiable. Do you follow Google Search Essentials? This one comes straight from Google’s hiring guidance. Since AI Overviews and AI Mode draw on the same index as Search, anything that breaks Google’s rules puts your AI visibility at risk too. What results do you expect, and in what timeframe? Also from Google’s list. You want a range and a reason, not a promise. We tell clients to expect directional wins in roughly six to eight weeks and measurable impact by around month three, and we explain what drives each. Will you share every change you make to my site? Google suggests asking this directly. The answer should be an unqualified yes, with a change log you can read without a login to the agency’s own tool. What access do you need during the audit? Google recommends giving read-only Search Console access while you evaluate an agency. If they need full admin rights to your site before you’ve signed anything, ask why. What does your off-site work actually involve? Ask for specifics: which kinds of publications, directories or communities, and how they earn placement. “We get you mentioned on Reddit” is not a plan. How do you connect AI visibility to leads or revenue? Citations are useful, but you’re paying for business outcomes. Ask how they track AI referral traffic and what they do about the visits that never click through. Can I talk to current clients? Google’s advice is to ask for examples and check references. Talk to someone who has been with them for at least two quarters, and ask whether reporting ever got uncomfortable and how the agency handled it. What happens to my data and accounts if we part ways? Every account, dashboard and tracking setup should be in your name or transferable to you. If the agency owns your analytics property, you’re renting your own history. Write the answers down. You’ll use them in the scorecard further down. What red flags should end the conversation? Walk away from any agency that guarantees citations or placements, sells “secret” AI files as the core of its service, or can’t show you a baseline. Each of those tells you something about how the agency will report to you later. Guaranteed citations or placements Google is direct about this: “No one can guarantee a #1 ranking on Google.” AI answers are generated fresh, vary by user and phrasing, and change as models update. An agency promising “guaranteed ChatGPT placement” is either measuring something trivial, like your brand name typed as the prompt, or setting up a report that flatters itself. “Secret” or proprietary AI files Some agencies sell special markup, hidden text, or AI-only files as the thing that gets you into AI answers. Google says no special optimizations are needed for AI Overviews and AI Mode. Files like llms.txt can be a reasonable low-cost addition for other AI tools, which we cover in our guide to llms.txt , but they are not a strategy and nobody should be charging you a premium for them. No baseline, no competitors If the first report shows you “now appearing in AI answers” without a before picture, there’s no way to know what the agency caused. The same goes for reports with no competitor context. Your mention share means one thing when your top competitor trails you and something very different when it’s named in nearly every answer. Activity dressed as outcome “We published 12 articles and made 200 optimizations” describes effort, not results. Reports should lead with what changed in mentions, citations, traffic and leads, then show the work that plausibly caused it. Shotgun off-site tactics Posting across forums for the sake of volume, sockpuppet accounts, invented author credentials and review schema on content that doesn’t contain reviews all fall in this bucket. Beyond the ethical problem, manufactured signals poison the measurement. If the agency created the citations, the report can’t tell you whether your brand actually earned visibility. How do you compare AI SEO agency proposals? Score each proposal on the same criteria, weight measurement and transparency most heavily, and don’t let price or polish override a weak score on either. The table below is built to paste into a spreadsheet: score each agency 1 to 5 on each line and multiply by the weight. Criterion Weight What a 5 looks like Agency A Agency B Agency C Named AI engines tracked 3 Lists each engine and explains the method Mentions and citations reported separately 3 Separate metrics, with competitor share Baseline before work starts 3 Sample baseline report provided Prompt set refreshed regularly 2 Quarterly review built into the plan Technical and content SEO depth 3 Specific examples of fixing site infrastructure Change log shared with you 3 Every change listed, readable by you Off-site plan is specific 2 Names source types and how placement is earned Ties visibility to leads or revenue 3 Shows AI referral tracking and conversion reporting Realistic timeline with reasoning 2 Ranges, not promises, with the why You own all accounts and data 3 Written into the agreement References from current clients 2 Two or more, willing to take a call No guarantees of placement 3 Says plainly that nobody can guarantee it Two quick notes on using it. First, any agency that scores a 1 on “no guarantees” or “you own all accounts” should be out regardless of the total. Second, score after the call, not during it, because a confident presenter can make a vague answer sound specific in the moment. It also helps to ask each agency which tools it uses for tracking and why. There are good options at different budgets, and we compare several in our roundup of the best AEO tools. An agency that can explain why it picked its stack, including the limits of that stack, usually understands the measurement problem well. What results should you expect from an AI SEO agency, and when? Expect early directional movement in mentions and citations within a couple of months and clearer business impact around the end of the first quarter, assuming the site’s technical foundation is in reasonable shape. Anyone promising dramatic results in two weeks is guessing, and anyone telling you to wait a full year before you see anything is padding the runway. In our AEO engagements, we typically see directional wins in about six to eight weeks and measurable impact by around month three. That’s a pattern, not a promise. It depends on how much infrastructure work the site needs, how competitive the category is, and how quickly changes can get published. Here’s how I’d think about the first 90 days. Period What should happen What you should see Weeks 1 to 2 Baseline across engines, prompt set agreed, technical and content audit A baseline report and a ranked list of fixes Weeks 3 to 6 Priority technical fixes, rewrites of the pages that should answer your top questions, first off-site outreach A change log and early shifts on specific prompts Weeks 7 to 12 Second wave of content, expanded off-site work, first quarterly review of prompts Mention and citation trends against baseline, AI referral traffic and leads Because AI answers vary, a single run of a single prompt tells you almost nothing. Look for trends across the full prompt set over several weeks. A good agency will tell you which movements it thinks are noise, which is the opposite of a report built to flatter. One last thing: the boring work is usually what moves the numbers. Fixing thin pages, cleaning up heading structure, making each page serve one clear purpose and rewriting key pages to answer questions directly will do more for your AI visibility than any new tactic you saw on LinkedIn this week. If an agency’s plan skips straight to the novel stuff, ask what it plans to do about the foundation. Frequently asked questions Is an AI SEO agency different from a regular SEO agency? It should be a regular SEO agency that also measures and works on AI visibility. AI search on Google uses the same index and the same eligibility rules as Search, so the skills overlap heavily; the differences are in prompt research, mention and citation tracking, and off-site work. Can an agency guarantee my brand will appear in ChatGPT? No. AI answers vary by phrasing, user and model version, and Google’s own hiring advice says no one can guarantee a top ranking. Treat any guarantee as a red flag about how the agency will report to you. How long does AI SEO take to show results? In our engagements, directional wins usually show up in about six to eight weeks, with measurable impact around month three. Sites that need heavy technical cleanup first can take longer. Do I need special AI files or schema to show up in AI Overviews? No. Google says there are no additional requirements or special optimizations needed for AI Overviews or AI Mode beyond being indexed and eligible to show with a snippet. What should I give an agency access to during evaluation? Read-only Search Console access is enough for an audit, which is what Google recommends. Save broader access for after you’ve signed and know who will be making changes. Want to see where you stand first?
